comment: Copy this to skills/<your-skill>/evals/evals.json and replace the
evaluations. Delete this comment block and the `note` fields when done.
Every evaluation is a prompt plus `skill_should_trigger`: true if your
skill should wake up for it, false if nothing in the catalog should. That
flag is the only place the expectation is written down -- no evaluation
names a skill, because the folder already says which one this is.
Write prompts the way a user would actually type them -- copying phrases
out of your SKILL.md description measures string matching, not routing.
If a prompt should trigger a DIFFERENT skill, put it in that skill's
dataset with true, rather than in yours with false. Routing installs the
whole catalog at once, so it is the same assertion either way, and false
keeps meaning 'nothing should fire'.
An evaluation with false is an id and a prompt. It is graded on one thing
-- that nothing fired -- so no skill is ever loaded for it and there is
nothing else to assert.
Tier 0 (required for every skill): at least 3 evaluations with true and 2
with false.
Tier 1 (required if your skill can be exercised on a generic runner): give
at least one evaluation an `expected_behavior` / `unexpected_behavior` /
`logs_contain` / `files_exist` expectation, so something grades what the
skill did and not just whether it fired.
Tier 2 (hardware or a live service): add skills/<your-skill>/evals/machine.yml
naming the kind of machine you need -- `runner_type` and/or `os`, nothing
else. Most skills do not need one.
Check your work without spending tokens:
python eval/run_evals.py --validate
Then run it for real:
python eval/run_evals.py --skill <your-skill>

evaluations.prompt: Something a user would say that should make this skill fire.
A different phrasing of the same need, with none of the same keywords.

evaluations.note: Tier 1. The same prompt grades routing AND what the agent then did.
evaluations.prompt: A task this skill should carry out end to end.
expected_behavior: A thing the agent must do, in plain language, graded by an LLM judge
unexpected_behavior: A mistake this skill exists to prevent

evaluations.note: Close to this skill's vocabulary but out of its scope: the wrong hardware, an adjacent domain, a question rather than a task.
evaluations.prompt: Something that sounds like this skill's territory but is not.
Another prompt that must not wake this skill up.
